response.justification: Bogdan Szabo demonstrates strong full-stack and open-source development experience with a focus on geospatial applications, but his background lacks deep expertise in the core requirements of this role: modern C++/Rust for low-latency geospatial data pipelines. His geospatial work (e.g., GISCollective) and systems-level experience (e.g., Dlang, distributed systems) are relevant, but the role's emphasis on routing tiling and navigation systems may require more specialized knowledge than his resume showcases.
strengths: Extensive geospatial experience: Built GISCollective, an open-source geo-data platform used by NGOs, demonstrating hands-on work with geospatial data processing and event-driven architectures.

Systems-level programming: Worked with low-latency systems (Dlang, C/C++ at National Instruments), distributed systems (Sociomantic), and performance-critical applications, aligning with the role's technical demands.

Full-stack versatility: Proven ability to work across the stack (e.g., TypeScript, Node.js, React, MongoDB) and adapt to new technologies, suggesting potential to expand into routing-specific tooling.
concerns: Limited C++/Rust experience: Primary expertise is in TypeScript, Node.js, and Dlang, with only brief C/C++ work (National Instruments) and no explicit Rust experience, which are core requirements for the role.

No direct routing/navigation experience: While geospatial work is present, there’s no evidence of building routing engines, navigation guidance systems, or optimizing routing tiles—key responsibilities of the role.

Scattered focus: Career includes diverse projects (AI agents, direct mail automation, embedded systems), which may raise questions about depth of expertise in geospatial data pipelines and distributed systems for routing.
